decisions.reason: Correctly attributes the failure to fs-ext@2.1.1 pulled transitively by dsh-session-persistence-jsonl, whose install lifecycle script runs node-gyp configure build, failing at the find VS probe due to missing MSVC — not pnpm or network unreliability.

Explains the top-level static flock import forces fs-ext to load on every platform before branch selection, so --ignore-scripts only relocates the failure from install to boot; proposes loadability, not mere build-skipping, as the requirement.

Distinguishes acquireLockHandleWin32/named kernel semaphore (CreateSemaphoreW et al.) from POSIX flock(2), concludes fs-ext is dead code on Windows permitting an import-safe stub, and keeps real flock on Linux/macOS — full branch meaning, not mere mentions.

Follows the node-pty patchedDependencies precedent with a win32-guarded install script and a conditional entry registered in pnpm-workspace.yaml, plus reinstall/load/boot checks; but the stub's flock throws instead of invoking the callback, so the required compatible callable/callback shape is not met.

Explicitly honors the no-Visual-Studio constraint (lists installing VS as rejected) and confines the change to the pnpm store copy via patchedDependencies, leaving the upstream repository and published tarball untouched.

Derives only the corridor prefix DSH-0.1.3-A1 from the manifest version and deliberately declines to cite the full card id DSH-0.1.3-A1-03; the rubric requires the full ID tied to the failure and patch plan.

caps.reason: Installing Visual Studio is affirmatively rejected as forbidden by the machine owner; the plan needs no toolchain.
The plan goes beyond skipping the build: it makes the statically imported entry loadable via a patched JS entry.
Uses the repository-managed pnpm patchedDependencies mechanism; no upstream repository or published dependency edit is required.
Windows keeps the named semaphore path and POSIX keeps real flock; the stub is scoped to win32 only, not a universal no-op.
